level1.title: Hello World
level1.description: Your first Pascal program – print 'Hello World!' and begin your programming journey.
level1.objective1: Understand the basic structure of a Pascal program
level1.objective2: Use the WriteLn procedure for text output

concept1.title: Program Structure
concept1.content: Every Pascal program starts with 'program Name;' and ends with 'end.'. The code between 'begin' and 'end.' is executed.

concept2.title: Text Output
concept2.content: WriteLn prints text to the screen. The text must be enclosed in single quotes.

level1.task: Write a program that outputs 'Hello World!'.

level2.title: Variables
level2.description: Learn how to declare and use variables in Pascal to store data.
level2.objective1: Use the 'var' section for variable declaration
level2.objective2: Create Integer variables for whole numbers

concept1.title: Variable Declaration
concept1.content: Variables are declared in the 'var' section. The format is: variableName: type;

concept2.title: Value Assignment
concept2.content: In Pascal, the assignment operator ':=' is used to assign a value to a variable.

level2.example1: Declaring and using an Integer variable
level2.task: Declare an Integer variable 'number', assign it the value 42, and output 'Number: 42'.

level3.title: Simple Math
level3.description: Perform arithmetic calculations and output the results.
level3.example1: Adding two numbers and outputting the result
level3.task: Calculate the sum of two numbers and output the result.

level4.title: Strings
level4.description: Work with text: learn the String data type and string concatenation.
level4.objective2: Output strings with commas in WriteLn

concept1.title: String Type
concept1.content: String stores text. Strings are written in single quotes: 'Example'

level4.example1: Using a String variable for output
level4.task: Declare a String variable and output it.

level5.title: Input and Output
level5.description: Interact with the user – learn to read and process input.
level5.objective1: Use Write for output without line break

concept1.title: Reading Input
concept1.content: ReadLn reads user input and stores it in a variable. Write outputs text without a line break.

level5.example1: A program that asks the user for their name
level5.task: Ask the user for their name and output a greeting.

level6.title: Conditions
level6.description: Make decisions in your program with if-then-else statements.
level6.objective3: Control program flow based on conditions

concept1.title: Conditional Statements
concept1.content: if checks a condition. If true, the then-block is executed, otherwise the else-block.

level6.example1: Checking if a number is positive or negative
level6.task: Check if an input number is positive or negative and output the result.

level7.title: For Loop
level7.description: Repeat code with the for-do loop for counting iterations.
level7.objective2: Use to and downto for counting up and down

concept1.title: For Loop Upward
concept1.content: for i := 1 to 5 do executes the code 5 times, with i counting from 1 to 5.

concept2.title: For Loop Downward
concept2.content: for i := 5 downto 1 do counts backwards from 5 to 1.

level7.task: Use a for loop to output the numbers from 1 to 5.

level8.title: While Loop
level8.description: Repeat code while a condition is true.

concept1.title: While Loop
concept1.content: while condition do repeats the code as long as the condition is true. Make sure to change the condition in the loop body!

level8.task: Use a while loop to output a countdown from 5 to 1.

level9.title: Procedures
level9.description: Structure your code with procedures for reusable code blocks.

concept1.title: Procedure Declaration
concept1.content: procedure Name(Parameter: Type) defines a procedure. Procedures execute code without returning a value.

level9.task: Create a procedure that takes a name as a parameter and outputs a greeting.

level10.title: Functions
level10.description: Create functions that calculate and return values.
level10.objective2: Set return values by assigning to function name

concept1.title: Function Declaration
concept1.content: function Name(Parameter: Type): ReturnType defines a function. The return value is set by assigning to the function name.

level10.example1: A function to calculate the square of a number
level10.task: Create a function that squares a number and returns the result.

level11.title: File I/O
level11.description: Learn to read from and write to files using Pascal's file handling commands.
level11.objective1: Use Assign to connect a variable to a file
level11.objective2: Use Reset, Rewrite, and Close for file operations
level11.objective3: Read and write data to text files

concept1.title: File Operations
concept1.content: Assign(f, 'filename') connects file variable f to a file. Rewrite creates a new file, Reset opens for reading, and Close closes the file.

level11.example1: Writing and reading a text file
level11.task: Write 'Hello World!' to a file using Assign, Rewrite, and Close.

level12.title: Sets
level12.description: Work with set data types and perform set operations.

concept1.title: Set Types
concept1.content: Sets are collections of elements of the same type. Define with 'set of' and use brackets: [1, 2, 3] or [1..10] for ranges.

level12.task: Create a set of prime numbers and check if 5 is in the set.

level13.title: Pointers
level13.description: Learn dynamic memory allocation with pointers and the New/Dispose commands.
level13.objective2: Use New to allocate memory and Dispose to free it

concept1.title: Pointer Basics
concept1.content: Pointers store memory addresses. Use New(p) to allocate memory and p^ to access the value at that address.

level13.example1: Using pointers to store and access values
level13.task: Create a pointer to an integer, allocate memory, assign value 42, and print it.

level14.title: Advanced Records
level14.description: Master variant records and nested record structures.

concept1.title: Nested Records
concept1.content: Records can contain other records as fields. Access nested fields with dot notation: record1.field1.subfield

level14.example1: Using nested records for complex data
level14.task: Create a TEvent record with a nested TDate record for the event date.

level15.title: Unit System
level15.description: Organize code into units/modules for better code management.
level15.objective2: Create procedures and functions in modules

concept1.title: Units Overview
concept1.content: Units are separate program modules with interface and implementation sections. They allow code reuse and organization.

level15.example1: Creating a utility module with procedures
level15.task: Create two procedures (Greet and Farewell) and call them.

helloWorld.title: Hello World
helloWorld.description: Your first Pascal program - the classic starting point.

arrayManipulation.title: Array Manipulation
arrayManipulation.description: Work with arrays to store and access multiple values.

recordUsage.title: Record Usage
recordUsage.description: Use records to organize related data.

bubbleSort.title: Bubble Sort
bubbleSort.description: Sort an array using the bubble sort algorithm.

primeCheck.title: Prime Check
primeCheck.description: Check if a number is prime.
